summary: Connect overview, intermediate landmark and close inspection through explicit scale cues and interruptible camera states, without pretending that a display-scale change preserves physical size relationships.
objective: A viewer can travel from a large setting to a small feature, understand each intermediate relationship and return without camera collision, model rescaling or hidden scale claims.
applies_when: A scene spans scales that cannot remain useful in one camera framing.
A close detail would lose its place in a city, body, machine or landscape.
intent_signals: move from city block to machine detail without losing context
zoom from whole body to tissue landmark
example_prompts: Travel from a factory overview through one machine to a bearing detail with interruptible stops.
Move from a watershed to a sensor site while disclosing any display exaggeration.
negative_signals: Uniformly scaling the world during focus and presenting distances as unchanged.
Teleporting directly to a detail with no identity or orientation cue.
not_for: One fixed hero close-up with a simple return action.

principles: Use at least one intermediate identity cue when the endpoints differ enough that direct motion loses orientation; the cue may be a landmark, locator volume, breadcrumb or retained inset.
Camera motion and display scaling are presentation state. Preserve true source/model coordinates and disclose any nonuniform display transform used to bridge scales.
Design each camera state for its viewport and purpose. The transition may cut, dissolve or move; it remains interruptible and has a deterministic return path.
implementation: In Blender, author named overview, intermediate and detail cameras/targets plus true-scale reference geometry. Exported cameras seed projections and transforms, not transition timing, safe areas or navigation state.

In Three.js, fit selected bounds using the installed PerspectiveCamera view-size/bounds behavior, update aspect/projection on resize, and pass each transition through the related interruptible-focus policy. Keep model transforms separate from camera/display transforms.
Retain a scale bar, known-size object, locator inset or explicit exaggeration badge at each state where size could be inferred. Store a breadcrumb of stable IDs and prior camera states.
observable_checks: Interrupt at the midpoint, choose another target and return: the last request wins, no stale transition snaps back, and source object transforms remain unchanged.

At every stop the selected feature is identifiable in its parent context. During continuous physically framed navigation, the camera does not unintentionally cross solid geometry; an authored cut, portal or scale transition may cross when clearly presented as a display-only transition.
Compare a displayed distance/size with source values: any separate scale factors are visible, while a true-scale state uses one declared factor.

creative_affordances: Use match cuts, portal frames, nested miniatures or continuous dolly moves to express the scale journey.
An intentionally disorienting reveal is valid when recovery and scale truth remain available afterward.
known_limits: PerspectiveCamera framing utilities do not supply collision avoidance, transition timing or truthful scale disclosure.
No camera transition, resize, collision or scale comparison was run.

claims.statement: Three.js PerspectiveCamera defines vertical field of view, aspect and clipping planes, can compute view bounds/size at a distance, supports sub-frustum view offsets, and requires updateProjectionMatrix after camera-property changes; glTF can transport a camera projection on a placed node and Blender 4.5 can export cameras.
claims.scope: Camera transport and current runtime framing primitives only; transition design, bounds fitting, collision and scale disclosure are application responsibilities.
